description: Private source contract only. No documentation endpoint, listener or SSO is enabled. Completed direct TLS 1.2+, exact configured Host/HTTPS Origin, canonical origin-form request, fresh Core Session and current exact-scope RBAC are mandatory. Read-only Deployment capability, approval catalog and management-scope requests require the cookie and explicit session channel; every mutation additionally requires the current CSRF proof. Authorization custody, encoded/alternate routing, Referer fallback, CORS and provider-token grants are forbidden. The reserved server is an example, never an operator default.

accountSessionCookie.name: __Host-mt_session
accountSessionCookie.description: One canonical nonzero Core mtas1 Account Session cookie. Fresh durable authentication, Deployment/recovery/generation and exclusive idle/absolute expiry checks apply. Never an IdP token, IaC credential or cached authority. Cookie issuance uses Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ and no Domain.

sessionCSRF.name: X-MeshTransit-CSRF
sessionCSRF.description: One <=256-byte dedicated mtscsrf1 intent proof bound to the complete current Session bearer, exact Origin and Deployment. Require together with the cookie for mutations. Preparation lifetime is 30-120 whole seconds, shortened to exclusive Session expiry; no future issue time, expiry equality or skew grace. The proof is replayable intent transport, never an operation/Session grant.

ConsoleOrigin.name: Origin
ConsoleOrigin.description: One exact operator-configured HTTPS Origin, including canonical non-default port when configured. Missing/null/foreign Origin rejects; Referer, forwarded headers and normalization never replace it.

ConsoleSessionProof.description: Shape hint only. Core verifies the complete canonical envelope/MAC and exact cookie/Origin/Deployment/time binding before fresh durable Session authentication.

display_code.description: Immutable display label. UUID remains the canonical API and authorization identity.

can_rename.description: Presentation hint only. Rename rechecks live ownership.

permissions.description: Workspace-level permissions the Session holds, for presentation only; every action reauthorizes.

display_code.description: Immutable display label. UUID remains the canonical API and authorization identity.

ConsoleDeploymentCapabilities.description: Navigation evidence only. Profiles share one feature set; limits come from the verified Deployment entitlement (ADR-050). Without an entitlement a self-hosted Deployment reports the single-Workspace baseline.

ownership.description: A member Device expires per profile and joins its owner's user groups; a Workspace Device never expires and survives staff changes.

owner.description: The owning member; null for a Workspace Device.

suspended_reason.description: admin: suspended by an administrator; handover: transferred to a member who has not yet signed in on the Device.

handover_to.description: The member a handover waits for.

dns_name.description: The Device's DNS name <label>.<workspace code>.<network code>.<suffix>, unique in the Network; null for a Device that holds no name (revoked or deleted). The suffix is the deployment's (default mesh.internal).

post.summary: Create a Workspace owned by the signed-in Account

Records are audit record v2, newest first; sealed records were rechecked by Core and a record whose seal does not recompute reports seal_mismatch. Without since/until the last 90 days are read. A window longer than 93 days is rejected as invalid_request; read older evidence window by window.

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound; default until minus 90 days

get.description: Requires audit.export on the Workspace (every stream in it) or on the Network named by network_id (that Network's stream only). Returns every record in the window oldest first, as stored, with no content filters, so a verifier sees whole runs of each stream and can check sequences and seal links offline with any implementation of seal v2 (see docs/protocol/audit-record-v2.md). At most 10000 records; a larger window answers audit_export_too_large. Without since/until the last 90 days are exported. A window longer than 93 days is rejected as invalid_request; read older evidence window by window.

Changes nothing. More than 20,000 active shares are refused with guardrail_impact_too_large; switching a guardrail to audit mode or deleting it needs no preview. While a guardrail of a Workspace is saved, offering, accepting or enabling a share of that Workspace answers a retryable conflict.

A Device waiting to be handed to the member stays suspended for an administrator. Lets tag owners without device_tag.read tag Devices.

Fresh Session and exact device.read Role Binding are mandatory on every page. UUIDv7 keyset pagination binds both scope IDs and inventory revision; a changed revision rejects continuation. Registration state is not online presence or packet authority. No keys, credentials, endpoints or provider claims are disclosed.

Requires device.transfer. To the Workspace: takes effect at once, the Device stops expiring and leaves its former owner's user groups. To a member (an active member of the Workspace and Network): the Device is suspended until that member signs in on it, which completes the handover.

get.description: Requires network.read. Lists the Workspace's members ordered by principal ID with their membership of this Network (null when they are not a member); pass next_after as after for the next page. Members of the Network are always listed; the rest of the Workspace only when the caller can add them (network.member.manage) or read the Workspace's members (member.read). can_manage reports network.member.manage. A suspended Workspace member is listed but cannot be added.

post.description: Requires network.member.manage (the owner, admin, or an it_admin of the Workspace or of this Network). Adds up to 150 active Workspace members, each named once; a member already in the Network is reported unchanged. A member of the Network can enroll Devices into it and receive Devices handed over in it. A suspended Workspace member cannot be added. Maps are not rebuilt.

200.description: The memberships created and the members already in the Network

post.summary: Remove a member from a Network
post.description: Requires network.member.manage. Nobody removes the owner or themselves, and the actor must outrank each role the member holds in its own scope: a Workspace-scope role needs the owner or a Workspace-scope admin or it_admin who could grant it; a role bound to this Network may also be outranked by the actor's admin or it_admin role bound to this Network; a custom role binding of this Network needs a Workspace-scope assigner. Each Device the member owns in this Network is moved to the Workspace, handed to another active member of this Network (suspended until that member signs in on it), or revoked as the plan says; a Device the plan does not name is revoked. A Device of this Network waiting to be handed to the member stays suspended for an administrator. The enrollment keys they issued for this Network are revoked, their roles for this Network end, and the Network membership is revoked; a browser registration they started is refused at approval. Their Workspace membership, Identity Groups, other Networks and Console sessions are unchanged.

new_owner_id.description: Required for transfer_member and absent otherwise

post.summary: Durably revoke the current Core Session
post.description: Require the current host-only Session cookie and a fresh proof bound to that exact cookie, Origin and Deployment. Atomically revoke only the matching active Session in the current recovery epoch, then expire only __Host-mt_session. Concurrent or completed revocation is an idempotent no-match. No provider token, upstream logout, alternate cookie, redirect or authority renewal is performed. JSON whitespace around the literal empty object is allowed.

204.description: The current Core Session is durably ended and its browser cookie is expired. The response has no body.

Set-Cookie.description: Exact host-only deletion for the Core Session cookie; no Domain or other cookie is changed.

schema.const: __Host-mt_session=; Path=/; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:01 GMT; Max-Age=0; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

default.description: Private pre-release failure leaves status/headers/body untouched. Authentication failures use the existing bounded management denial without clearing or renewing cookies. Durable submission failure is uncertain delivery, never non-commit evidence or an automatic retry.

post.summary: End every Core Session of the signed-in Account
post.description: Require the current host-only Session cookie and a fresh proof bound to that exact cookie, Origin and Deployment. Atomically advance the Account's session generation and end every active Core Session of the Account in every Workspace, including the current one, then expire only __Host-mt_session. Devices are not affected. A Session that another sign-out already ended gets the bounded authentication denial and ends nothing. No provider token, upstream logout, alternate cookie, redirect or authority renewal is performed. JSON whitespace around the literal empty object is allowed.

Every inventory read and management action rechecks its exact permission and scope. No CSRF proof, request body, Authorization credential, Session identifier or provider claim is accepted or returned.

post.description: Consume shared source/Session budgets and freshly authenticate the existing cookie before independent OS entropy. Return only the proof and exclusive expiry. No Set-Cookie, provider token, identity or resource grant. JSON whitespace around the literal empty object is allowed. Existing private transport/body/header/cookie/capacity/deadline bounds and zero-output pre-release failure apply.

The Session version increments, so requests still bound to the previous Workspace fail their exact-version check and the Console reloads its scope. Switching to the current Workspace returns replayed true and changes nothing. A committed switch appends one audit record.

Listing grants nothing; every management action rechecks its own permission.

The projection is for Console navigation and route guards only. It grants no Workspace, platform, billing or operation authority; unknown, cloud, contradictory or stale authority fails closed.
